deep.reconstruction:
This folio contains no derivations, formulas or computations. It is a sequence of aphoristic notes from Hilbert's notebooks (Cod. Ms. Hilbert 600), continuing the reflections on the nature of mathematics from the previous page. There is nothing to reconstruct mathematically. The content, block by block:

(1) An image of mathematical labour. Lie, 'with Norwegian giant's hand', may have broken the blocks out of the marble cliffs. The harder, finer and deeper artist's work was done by the function theorists Riemann, Weierstrass and Cauchy. The arithmetician (number theorist) finds even this too coarse, and accepts the results of function theory with equanimity. This is a ranking: Lie's transformation-group theory is coarse but grand; complex function theory is finer; arithmetic is finest. It fits Hilbert's number-theoretic period of the 1890s (Zahlbericht, class fields). The next page explicitly celebrates the 'marriage' of number theory and function theory in class field theory / complex multiplication.

(2) Hilbert modifies 'the well-known saying'. Often one can say with more right: 'Formulas are there to hide thoughts.' The original is Talleyrand's dictum that speech was given to man to disguise his thoughts.

(3) 'Jacobi and Kummer were the greatest calculators (Rechner) and will remain so forever.'

(4) Three kinds of scientific pleasure:
- new, unexpected positive facts;
- eliminating old prejudices, conscious and unconscious;
- overcoming old conjectures stated in the literature, and particular difficulties.

(5) On exactness. The mathematician wants precise statements everywhere, above all also where he does applied mathematics; such statements are also easier to grasp. Hence in physics he wants exact limit procedures ('Grenzausführungen'), not approximations. 'Infinitely small is = 0.' One should not imagine physical quantities as small, nor even relatively small (continued on the next page). This continues the previous page's point: the mathematical limit plays the role of a Kantian regulative idea, i.e. an exact physical law that exists only in us.
errors: No mathematical errors are possible; the page has no mathematical claims beyond philosophical slogans.

'Unendlichklein ist = 0' is a methodological slogan in the Weierstrassian epsilon-limit spirit, not a theorem. It rejects actual infinitesimals; it is consistent with the previous page's demand to enclose quantities in finite bounds before passing to the limit.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is purely aphoristic and contains no mathematics. The views fit well-known Hilbert attitudes: high esteem for number theory, preference for rigor and exact limits, and his famous wit. Some of these notebook aphorisms have been quoted in the secondary literature. The Lie metaphor and the formula variant of Talleyrand's saying are charming details but not surprising.
transcription_corrections: Line 'Alte Vorurteile bewusste und unbewusste, beseitigen': the image reads with a comma, 'Alte Vorurteile, bewusste und unbewusste, beseitigen' (the first comma is faint).

Item 3: the interlinear insertion 'in der Litteratur ausgesprochene' is written below the line under 'Alte) Vermuthungen'. A bracket after 'Alte' marks where it is inserted, so the reading 'Alte in der Litteratur ausgesprochene Vermuthungen' is correct. The struck letter before 'überwinden' looks like a capital 'U'/'Ü' rather than 'ü'.
'{+auch+}' is inserted above the line between 'vor Allem,' and 'wo er angewandte Mathematik treibt' — correct as given.
The struck character after '3 Arten' is an unclear crossed-out letter (possibly 'd' or 'x'); the transcription's '[-x-]' is acceptable.
'Grenzausführungen' looks right from the image ('genaue Grenzausführungen erwünscht').
'Jakobi' is Hilbert's spelling of Jacobi; it is kept as written.
